title: The orchestrator and its agents
text: Agents The orchestrator and its agents One orchestrator and four memory-augmented subagents integrate two ontologies. Every question a subagent asks goes to the cheapest tier that can settle it. On this page Subagents Routing Recalibration Running it Cost Subagents flowchart LR S["Source + target ontology"] --> K["KROMA: matching"] K --> V["Validation: remove conflicts"] V --> R["Reasoning: place unmatched classes"] S --> E["Extraction: missing edges"] K -.questions.-> C{{"Orchestrator"}} E -.questions.-> C R -.questions.-> C C --> T1["Evidence"] C --> T2["Local model"] C --> T3["API model"] V --> B[("Blackboard")] R --> B E --> B Subagent Asks Answers Evidence it brings KromaAgent (KROMA) Is this source class the same as this target class? yes, no Character n-gram similarity of names, plus agreement of already matched parents ExtractionAgent How does this class relate to this candidate? subClassOf , part_of , none Label rules (a head word gives subClassOf , a modifier gives part_of ) and the parents of similar classes ReasoningAgent Under which candidate does this unmatched class belong? a candidate code, or none The counterparts of its nearest matched ancestors, and their descendants two levels down ValidationAgent (asks nothing) removes the weaker side of each conflict One-to-many matches and criss-cross matches that would collapse a hierarchy KROMA settles exact label and synonym matches first, and never asks again about a class it settled, which is KROMA's refinement step in this setting. Tied conflicts go to a review queue for a person. Routing Evidence. At or above accept , the question takes the answer the evidence supports; at or below reject , the fallback. No model is called. Local model. The rest go to the local model in batches of 8; an answer with confidence at least local_trust is kept. API model. The rest go to the API model in batches of 20, while the Budget (calls or list-price dollars) lasts. Past it, the local answer stands and the decision is marked budget . A model that fails or leaves a question out of its reply does not stop the run: the question falls back to the next answer available. Recalibration Every escalated question the local model also answered is a labeled example of how far the local model can be trusted. Escalations alone only show the local model's unsure answers, so the controller also audits a random 10% of the answers it would keep, asking the API model too. Questions are settled in rounds of 160; after each round, local_trust becomes the lowest confidence at which the local model agreed with the API model at least 90% of the time, over at least 10 examples, or NEVER (above 1) when no confidence qualifies, so every question the evidence does not settle goes up until the comparisons bring the threshold back down. Each change is written to the blackboard's log. Running it from agentic_ontologist.workflow import Budget, ClaudeCodeModel, Controller, OllamaModel, Workflow, load_owl source, target = load_owl("data/MouseHuman/mouse.owl"), load_owl("data/MouseHuman/human.owl") controller = Controller(local=OllamaModel("llama3.1"), api=ClaudeCodeModel("claude-sonnet-5-5"), budget=Budget(api_calls=20)) result = Workflow(controller).integrate(source, target, place=100) print(len(result.matches), result.validation.removed, result.tiers) Cost Every model call is recorded on agentic_ontologist.costs.METER with its tokens, seconds, and list-price dollars. experiments/agentic_workflow compares the routed policy with a local model alone, an API model alone, a call cap, and evidence alone, on all three tasks; see Experiments and the live showcase . Previous Overview Next Getting started

title: Architecture
text: Design Architecture The installable package is isolated under src/agentic_ontologist/ . Everything else is support material. On this page System overview Integration pipeline Package map Algorithm extension points Vector retrieval Retrieval plugins Memory and cache Shared memory Agent runtime Agent tools Extension patterns System overview flowchart LR Input["OWL / RDF / JSON-LD"] --> Parser["Parser"] CLI["CLI or Python API"] --> Workspace["OntologyWorkspace"] Parser --> Ontology["Ontology"] Workspace --> Parser Ontology --> Refine["Refinement"] Refine --> Graph["ConceptGraph or Hypergraph"] Graph --> Embed["Graph + text embeddings"] Embed --> Retrieve["Vector and web retrieval"] Retrieve --> Agent["Agent runtime"] Agent --> Validate["Validation + UQ"] Validate --> Output["Matches, answers, traces"] classDef boundary fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,color:#1f2328; classDef core fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da,color:#1f2328; class Input,CLI,Output boundary; class Parser,Workspace,Ontology,Refine,Graph,Embed,Retrieve,Agent,Validate core; The path-based API and CLI share the same parser, graph, retrieval, and reasoning components. Experiments orchestrate this pipeline without entering the library layer. Integration pipeline 1. Matching (KROMA) Exact label and synonym matches, then near names, decided by evidence or a model. 2. Validation Remove one-to-many and criss-cross conflicts; queue ties for review. 3. Reasoning Place classes with no match under the target hierarchy, from their matched ancestors. 4. Extraction Propose the subClassOf and part_of edges an ontology is missing. The orchestrator in agentic_ontologist.workflow routes every subagent's questions; see Agents . Package map Module Responsibility cli.py and workspace.py Path-based terminal commands and reusable ontology query sessions agents/core/ Agent orchestration, typed events, and tool execution agents/decisions.py Optional Jev model routing and tool-risk gating, recorded on the existing trace agents/runtime/ Execution traces, a local DuckDB file, or DynamoDB persistence agents/ontology_of_thought/ Conversation memory, thought graphs, optimization, and reconstruction agents/tools/ Shared registry plus ontology, knowledge-graph, and website providers algorithms/graph/ Ontology, concept, graph, hypergraph, predicates, and shared builders algorithms/refinement/ Relation, ontology, offline graph, and online stream refinement algorithms/views/ Hypergraph and multigraph analysis adapters parser/ One format-selecting facade over RDF, JSON, and text adapters; RDF schema declarations stay outside the concept graph memory/ Query cache: hot questions, short-term concept sets, and long-term patterns routing/ Harness of typed questions that replays a cached question or continues into retrieval memory_store.py Saved concept embeddings, separate from the query cache embeddings/encoders/ Text and Node2Vec graph encoders embeddings/vector_index/ Backend-neutral vector search with an exact Torch implementation retrieval/ Structural sampling, web and vector retrieval, and an optional Jev context harness functions/similarity/ Cosine, normalized web distance, hybrid, and cross-graph scoring prompting/ Typed ontology-equivalence prompts and machine-readable answer parsing validation/ Alignment metrics, validation rules, tuple evaluation, pipelines, and ontology linting uq/ Dependency-free agreement scoring and optional UQLM, graph, and ensemble backends integrations/memcommit/ Shared agent memory on MemCommit : run traces, the answer cache as a view of the store, the declared memory structure, and an OntoDB storage engine Algorithm extension points Graph domain Extend focused models or use OntologyStructureBuilder to construct new graph representations. Relation refinement Configure RelationRefiner with a RuleSet and inspect its structured result. Ontology refinement Use OntologyRefiner to refine, rebuild, and preserve ontology metadata. Offline graph refinement Use OfflineGraphRefiner for deter

title: What is the heart part of?
text: Demo What is the heart part of? A local chat over the adult mouse anatomy ontology. Local llama3.1 chat over data/MouseHuman/mouse.owl . LLM_MODEL=ollama:llama3.1 agonto chat data/MouseHuman/mouse.owl Loaded swift-bison-3418: 3089 concepts, 3202 relations. The first question builds embeddings, saves them, and later runs reuse that memory. Delete saved embeddings with: agonto memory clear data/MouseHuman/mouse.owl Progress is shown below. Type 'exit' to stop. agonto> What is the heart part of? Building the concept graph from 3089 concepts. Loading the text embedding model. The first run may download it. Learning graph structure embeddings. Embedding concepts: 3089/3089 Embedded 3089 concepts. Saved 3089 concept embeddings to results/memory/mouse-plain-93756393d6306c8f. Connecting to ollama:llama3.1. Retrieving concepts related to the question. Asking ollama:llama3.1. Waiting for the model to answer. ▶ Run d7fb9bdd-73d1-4e73-9f57-c2919b363b75 started 🧠 LLM request → llama3.1: You are given an ontology developing task and a list of available tools. - Task: QUERY: What is the heart part of? RELEVANT CONCEPT CLUSTERS: 1. heart ventricle muscular part 2. right ventricle muscular part 3. heart right atrium 4. heart right ventricle 5. cardiac muscle 6. heart apex 7. left ventricle muscular part 8. heart ventricle 9. heart valve 10. fourth ventricle KEY RELATIONS (within top-k): - heart right ventricle --(2.0)--> heart ventricle - left ventricle muscular part --(2.0)--> heart ventricle muscular part - right ventricle muscular part --(2.0)--> heart ventricle muscular part TASK: Using the above concept clusters and relations as contextual guidance, answer the user query precisely. Prefer concepts and relations that appear in the RELEVANT CONCEPT CLUSTERS and KEY RELATIONS. Cite specific terms. - Tools list: {"ontology_term_info": {"tool_name": "ontology_term_info", "module_path": "agentic_ontologist.agents.tools.ontology.ontology_lookup", "tool_type": "module", "arguments": {"term": ["head"], "ontologies": [], "exact": false, "max_results": 5, "include_fields": ["label", "synonyms", "description", "iri", "short_form", "ontology_prefix", "xrefs", "aliases", "annotations", "definitions"]}, "aliases": []}, "search_term_context": {"tool_name": "search_term_context", "module_path": "agentic_ontologist.agents.tools.website.website_lookup", "tool_type": "module", "arguments": {"term": ["mouse", "head", "anatomy"], "top_k": 5, "site_filters": [], "include_wikipedia": true, "region": null, "time_range": null, "max_chars": 4000}, "aliases": []}, "search_knowledge_graph": {"tool_name": "search_knowledge_graph", "module_path": "agentic_ontologist.agents.tools.knowledge_graph.knowledge_graph_lookup", "tool_type": "module", "arguments": {"term": ["heart septum"], "top_k": 5, "include_public": null, "only_kgs": null, "max_merged": null, "opts": null}, "aliases": []}} ------------------------ Instructions: - Answer naturally if no tool is required. - For ontology labels, synonyms, descriptions, or aliases, use ontology_term_info. - For a general web lookup, use search_term_context. - When using a tool, return only a JSON object with tool_name, tool_type, arguments, and module_path. - Do not invent arguments or fields. 🧠 LLM response: To answer the user query "What is the heart part of?", I will look for relevant concepts in the provided concept clusters. From the RELEVANT CONCEPT CLUSTERS, I see that there are several concepts related to the heart, such as "heart ventricle muscular part", "right ventricle muscular part", and "heart right atrium". However, none of these directly answer the question "What is the heart part of?". Looking at the KEY RELATIONS, I notice a relation between "heart right ventricle" and "heart ventricle" with a confidence score of 2.0. This suggests that the heart right ventricle is a part of the heart ventricle. Using this information, I will use the ontology_term_info tool to look up the concept "heart ventricle muscular part"

title: Experiments
text: Evaluation Experiments Run versioned JSON suites and retain readable, reproducible results without mixing generated artifacts into the library. On this page The orchestrator on Mouse–Human Start with the smoke benchmark Hosted tracking Compare context selection Fetch benchmark data Inspect before running Run Maintained ablations Local artifacts The orchestrator on Mouse–Human experiments/agentic_workflow runs each subagent on the OAEI anatomy track under five routing policies. Answers are shared across policies, and each policy is charged for the questions it asked. Policy Matching F1 Extraction precision / recall Reasoning correct / exact API calls API spend Routed 0.913 0.617 / 0.567 0.25 / 0.24 97 $0.96 Routed, capped 0.855 0.533 / 0.433 0.25 / 0.24 30 $0.30 Local only (llama3.1) 0.823 0.276 / 0.293 0.19 / 0.19 0 $0 API only (claude-sonnet-5-5) 0.924 0.740 / 0.620 0.43 / 0.36 108 $1.11 Evidence only 0.839 0.800 / 0.367 0.42 / 0.34 0 $0 With llama3.1 as the local tier, audits show it disagrees with the API model too often, so the orchestrator stops trusting it and routing saves little beyond the free evidence tier. Reasoning has fewer questions than one recalibration round, so the routed policy kept llama3.1's placements there. Every decision is in the showcase . python experiments/agentic_workflow/run.py --json results/agentic_workflow/2026-10-18.json python showcase/build.py results/agentic_workflow/2026-10-18.json Start with the smoke benchmark ./scripts/run_experiments.sh smoke ./scripts/run_experiments.sh smoke cat results/experiments/smoke/summary.md This fast benchmark compares baseline relation normalization with structural refinement, then reports their precision, recall, and F1. It requires no LLM, network access, or model download. On the second run, the report marks each variant reproducible when its metric fingerprint matches the previous run for the same configuration and source revision. Hosted tracking uv sync --extra tracking uv run wandb login ./scripts/run_experiments.sh smoke --tracker wandb The Agentic Ontologist publishes a comparison table, scalar metrics, logs, manifests, and generated figures to Weights & Biases. Temporary local artifacts are deleted after a successful upload. Set WANDB_PROJECT and optional WANDB_ENTITY to choose the destination, or add --keep-local to retain both copies. Hosted artifacts can contain ontology-derived output. Use a private W&B project and confirm your data policy before enabling remote tracking. Compare context selection ./scripts/run_experiments.sh context This local comparison scores the same retrieved shortlist with passthrough context and a shadow Jev policy. It reports selection precision, recall, F1, returned context size, and rejection rate without calling the Jev API. Live Jev scoring remains opt-in through AGONTO_CONTEXT_HARNESS=jev . Fetch benchmark data git lfs install git lfs pull Bundled OWL, RDF, Turtle, and model artifacts use Git LFS. Fetch them before running maintained suites; dry runs do not require the data. Inspect before running ./scripts/run_experiments.sh quickstart --dry-run ./scripts/run_experiments.sh ablations --dry-run Run # Quick comparison ./scripts/run_experiments.sh quickstart # All maintained ablations ./scripts/run_experiments.sh ablations # One experiment ./scripts/run_experiments.sh ablations --select with-uq The equivalent direct command is python -m experiments CONFIG.json . The shell entry point resolves named maintained suites and uses the repository environment. title: Getting started
text: Setup Getting started Install the Agentic Ontologist, inspect an ontology, and query it directly from the terminal. On this page Install Configure Inspect an ontology Search locally Ask questions Run the evaluation pipeline Select retrieval backends Route models and gate tools Verify Install git clone https://github.com/lamng3/agentic-ontologist.git cd agentic-ontologist ./setup.sh source .venv/bin/activate For a smaller installation, select only the provider integrations you need: uv venv --python 3.12 source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e ".[openai,knowledge-graph,dev]" Configure cp .env.example .env Set one model provider and any retrieval services required by your workflow. Purpose Variables Model LLM_MODEL , one provider API key Ontology lookup BIOPORTAL_API_KEY Web lookup TAVILY_API_KEY Google CSE counts GOOGLE_API_KEY , GOOGLE_CSE_CX Knowledge graph NEO4J_URI , NEO4J_USER , NEO4J_PASSWORD Thought storage DYNAMO_TABLE , AWS credentials, or AGONTO_DYNAMO_DISABLED=1 Jev decisions JEV_API_KEY , then any of AGONTO_CONTEXT_HARNESS , AGONTO_MODEL_ROUTING , AGONTO_TOOL_GATE Inspect an ontology agonto inspect data/my-ontology.owl agonto inspect data/my-ontology.ttl --json inspect parses local OWL, RDF/XML, Turtle, N-Triples, TriG, TriX, or JSON-LD without loading an embedding or language model. Search locally agonto search data/my-ontology.owl \ "water quality measurement" --top-k 8 This builds the concept graph and returns the most relevant ontology concepts. The first run may download the configured text embedding model. Ask questions # One question agonto query data/my-ontology.owl \ "Which concepts describe freshwater temperature?" # Interactive terminal session agonto chat data/my-ontology.owl The ontology is parsed and embedded once per command, before the first question. Interactive mode reuses that graph for every question in the session. Add --refine to apply relation refinement first. Answers are plain sentences. Add --log to print the detailed run, or type log after an answer. For a local model, set LLM_MODEL=ollama:llama3.1 . Hosted models require the corresponding API key. The Ollama client is installed with the Agentic Ontologist. search , query , and chat save concept embeddings under results/memory and load them on the next run. Delete that store with agonto memory clear data/my-ontology.owl . Pass --no-save-memory to skip writing it. Answers are cached separately under results/cache . The architecture page describes the hot, short-term, and long-term tiers and how eviction keeps each one inside its cap. Run the evaluation pipeline agonto run --ontology envo sweet --top_k 10 --eval_alignment agonto run --ontology envo sweet --eval_alignment --refine Catalog-based evaluation output is written under results/runs/ . Select retrieval backends from agentic_ontologist.retrieval import create_vector_index, create_web_search web = create_web_search("mediawiki") index = create_vector_index("torch-exact", dimension=768) Use static or dataset for deterministic offline work. Register project-specific web, ANN, DiskANN, or vector-database adapters through the same public retrieval API. Optional Jev context selection is separate from retrieval. Install it with uv sync --extra jev , set JEV_API_KEY , and enable AGONTO_CONTEXT_HARNESS=jev . It starts in shadow mode and fails open to the original shortlist. Route models and gate tools Model routing and tool-risk gating use the same Jev key. They stay off until enabled, and they do not change which evidence the context harness selects. uv sync --extra jev export JEV_API_KEY=your_typesafe_api_key export AGONTO_MODEL_ROUTING=jev export AGONTO_ROUTE_LOCAL=ollama:phi3 export AGONTO_ROUTE_CAREFUL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B export AGONTO_TOOL_GATE=jev Decision What Jev chooses If Jev cannot decide Model routing local for short lookups, standard for normal ontology questions, careful for alignment, conflicts, and multi-ontology reasoning. title: Route each question to the cheapest model that can settle it
text: Route each question to the cheapest model that can settle it The Agentic Ontologist is an orchestrator and four memory-augmented subagents (KROMA for matching, extraction, reasoning, and validation) that integrate ontologies, each question routed to the cheapest model that can settle it. Around them, a toolkit loads an ontology, retrieves nearby concepts, and answers with a language model. $ git clone https://github.com/lamng3/agentic-ontologist.git && cd agentic-ontologist $ ./setup.sh && source .venv/bin/activate $ agonto chat ontology.owl Get started Playground Agents Showcase Quality against cost one recorded run Try it: Pick a task to compare routing policies, then press Another to watch a real question get settled. Watch one question get settled Another The numbers and the decisions are from the recorded run on (ollama:llama3.1 and claude-sonnet-5-5), the same file as the showcase . The page computes nothing. title: Leaderboard
text: Results Leaderboard Every routing policy of the recorded run, ranked by quality for each agent, with what it spent. The routed policy sends each question to the cheapest tier that can settle it. The board shows what that costs in quality: on matching it trails only the policy that pays the API model for everything, and spends less. Other policies are the alternatives it was compared with: local model only, API model only, evidence only, and routing under a cap on API calls. How to read it Quality is the headline metric of each agent: F1 after repair for matching, precision for extraction, and correct placements for reasoning. API spend is list price, and each policy is charged only for the questions it asked. Local and evidence-only policies spend nothing. Click a column to sort. Ranks stay with quality, so a sort does not change who is first. The showcase shows every decision behind these numbers. Previous Experiments Next Reference

title: Playground
text: Try it Playground Pick a class of the mouse anatomy ontology and see what the matching agent's evidence tier does with it: its nearest human classes, their evidence, and whether the controller would settle each pair or ask a model. What runs where Everything runs in your browser, on the two real ontologies of the Mouse–Human track. The Agentic Ontologist itself is Python and is not run here: this page recomputes the evidence tier with a port of its name index (TF-IDF over character n-grams, as scikit-learn computes it) and of the matching agent's retrieval and the controller's rule, and checks the result against the Python. The local and API models are not hosted: Ask my model uses a model you run: Ollama on this computer is detected automatically, or you can load a tiny model that runs in your browser on WebGPU (a few hundred megabytes, kept by your browser), or point it at another endpoint. Loading the playground… How to read it A class that shares a normalized name with a human class is settled by exact name and never asked about again. About 1,100 of the mouse classes are. For every other class the agent asks about its nearest candidates (k of them) whose similarity reaches the floor. Parents that were matched exactly add a small bonus when they agree. The controller settles a pair by evidence at or above Accept (yes) or at or below Floor (no). The rest go to a local model, then to an API model. That is the routing the showcase measures; the last column shows what the recorded run did with each pair. What is not here The local and API tiers, batching, recalibration, and the budget are not run. Ask my model sends one pair with the controller's instruction, which is simpler than the controller's batch prompt. Extraction, reasoning, and validation are not run; see Agents . When two candidates have exactly the same similarity at the cutoff, Python's sort and this page's can keep different ones. Their evidence is identical, so the routing is too.

title: Reference
text: Commands Reference Commands, extension points, and environment variables. On this page Command-line interfaces Supported ontology inputs Public extension points Repository layout Jev environment Security Authors Command-line interfaces agonto --help agonto inspect ONTOLOGY.owl agonto search ONTOLOGY.owl "natural-language text" agonto query ONTOLOGY.owl "question" agonto chat ONTOLOGY.owl [--log] agonto memory clear ONTOLOGY.owl agonto run --help agonto-hypergraph --help agonto-lint ONTOLOGY.ttl ./scripts/run_experiments.sh SUITE --dry-run Supported ontology inputs The path-based CLI detects OWL/RDF XML ( .owl , .rdf , .xml ), Turtle, N3, N-Triples, TriG, TriX, and JSON-LD. Use --format when a file extension is ambiguous. Public extension points API Purpose create_web_search(name, **options) Select static, dataset, MediaWiki, Google CSE, or a registered provider register_web_search(plugin, factory) Add a visible project-specific search provider create_vector_index(name, **options) Create exact, ANN, DiskANN, or vector-database indexes register_vector_index(name, factory) Register a vector-index adapter OnlineOntologyRefiner.refine(graph, updates) Apply streamed ontology updates and return deferred validation cases Parser(path).to_ontology() Parse supported RDF or relation-dataset formats through one facade create_model_router() Choose local , standard , or careful once per run when AGONTO_MODEL_ROUTING=jev create_tool_gate() Block configured external tool calls when AGONTO_TOOL_GATE=jev Repository layout src/agentic_ontologist/ Installable library tests/ Automated tests examples/ Runnable examples experiments/ Runner and maintained configurations scripts/ Maintained experiment entry points data/ Ontology and benchmark data docs/ This static instruction website results/ Ignored generated artifacts Jev environment Variable Purpose JEV_API_KEY TypeSafe key. Copied to TYPESAFE_API_KEY when that variable is empty. AGONTO_CONTEXT_HARNESS Set to jev to score retrieved context. AGONTO_CONTEXT_MODE is shadow or live . AGONTO_MODEL_ROUTING Set to jev to route each run. Pair with AGONTO_ROUTE_LOCAL , AGONTO_ROUTE_STANDARD , and AGONTO_ROUTE_CAREFUL . AGONTO_TOOL_GATE Set to jev to gate tools. AGONTO_GATED_TOOLS lists names, and AGONTO_TOOL_RISK_THRESHOLD defaults to 0.5 . Routing fails open to LLM_MODEL . An enabled tool gate fails closed for gated tools only. Query text and redacted tool arguments are sent to TypeSafe. Decisions appear on the existing trace as model.routed and tool.blocked . Security pre-commit run --all-files gitleaks git --config .gitleaks.toml Store credentials only in .env . Never place secrets in source, experiment configs, logs, manifests, or data files.
